before.description_long:
ElevenLabs is a voice-focused AI company best known for realistic text-to-speech and voice cloning. Beyond TTS it now spans audiobooks, music generation and voice agents, making it one of the more complete audio stacks available to developers and creators.

The current model is Eleven v3, which hit general availability in February 2026. Compared with the older Multilingual v2, v3 substantially expanded language coverage and added the Eleven v3 Conversational model built for voice agents, which can clone a voice from just a few seconds of audio. Around the same time the company launched ElevenMusic with a Music Marketplace for creator monetization, and ElevenReader, an audiobook product at $11/mo positioned against Audible.

Core capabilities include high-quality multilingual TTS, instant and professional voice cloning, real-time conversational agents, music generation and an API with its own subscription tiers for production use.

Pricing runs from Free ($0/mo, 10k credits, roughly 10 minutes of TTS, no commercial rights and required attribution) up through Starter ($6/mo, commercial rights and instant cloning), Creator ($22/mo, professional cloning and 192kbps, often promoted at $11 for the first month), Pro ($99/mo), Scale ($299/mo, 3 seats), Business ($990/mo, 10 seats) and custom Enterprise. Annual billing gives two months free.

The main limitations are credit-based usage that can run out quickly on higher-volume work, no commercial rights or required attribution on the free plan, and costs that climb fast once you need many hours of audio or several seats. Voice cloning also raises consent and misuse concerns you have to manage yourself.

ElevenLabs suits creators, studios and developers who need natural-sounding voices in many languages, teams building voice agents, and anyone producing audiobooks or narration at scale. The company reached roughly $500M ARR by April 2026 and raised a $500M Series D at an $11B valuation, with a secondary sale in July 2026 reportedly targeting around $22B.

before.description_long:
Kling AI is a video generation platform built by the Chinese company Kuaishou. You describe a scene in text, or feed it a still image, and it animates a short cinematic clip. Over the past two years it has grown from an experimental demo into one of the most widely used AI video tools.

The current version is Kling 3.0, which launched on February 5, 2026 on the Omni One architecture. It added native multilingual audio, multi-shot storyboarding of up to six connected shots, and output up to 4K at 60fps, alongside better character consistency and an improved Motion Brush. On June 17, 2026 Kuaishou followed up with Kling 3.0 Turbo, a faster and cheaper mode with synced audio starting around 0.8 yuan per second at 720p, plus a 3.0 Omni upgrade that brought 4K editing and 3-15 second durations.

In practice the strengths are motion quality, prompt adherence and the ability to string several shots into a coherent sequence rather than one isolated clip. The Kling 3.0 Pro model topped the ArtificialAnalysis text-to-video leaderboard in February 2026 with an Arena ELO of 1240.

Pricing is freemium. The free tier gives 66 credits a day (reset daily, no rollover, watermarked, roughly 5-second clips). Paid monthly plans run about $10/mo for Standard (660 credits), $37/mo for Pro (3,000 credits), $92/mo for Premier (8,000 credits) and $180/mo for Ultra (26,000 credits). Annual billing cuts roughly 34% off Standard through Premier, bringing the effective monthly cost to around $6.60, $24.42 and $60.72; Ultra has no annual option.

The main limitations are clip length and cost. Even the top plans generate clips of up to about 15 seconds, not minutes, so longer videos have to be assembled from multiple generations. Credits also drain quickly at higher resolutions, and the free tier's watermark and short clips make it more of a trial than a working tool.

Kling suits creators, marketers and video editors who want high-quality short clips for social content, ads or B-roll, and who are comfortable working shot by shot rather than expecting one long finished video.

before.description_long:
Krea AI is a web-based creative platform that started as a real-time image generation tool and has grown into a broader suite covering image, video, 3D, and upscaling. It combines its own models with a library of third-party ones, letting users move between styles and tasks without leaving the browser.

The current flagship is Krea 2, released in May 2026 as the company's first foundation image model built from scratch, described as a Diffusion Transformer. It was followed in June 2026 by Krea 2 Turbo, which generates high-quality images in roughly two seconds. Krea also published open-weights versions of the model, Krea-2-Raw and Krea-2-Turbo, on Hugging Face under a custom license, and a Krea 2 API is available for developers.

On top of the base models, Krea 2 adds Generative Sliders, launched in June 2026, for direct control over intensity, complexity, movement, and prompt creativity, LoRA training so users can teach it their own style or subject, and a Moodboard Gallery. The wider platform also includes text- and image-to-video generation, 3D generation, AI upscaling, and newer additions such as a Krea Agent, App Builder, and Nodes Agent for building automated workflows.

Pricing is tiered and metered in compute units. The free plan costs nothing and gives 100 units per day with no credit card required, though it has no video generation and upscaling is capped at 2K. Pro is $35 per month, or $21 per month billed yearly, with 20,000 units, image and video concurrency, all video models, and a commercial license. Max is $105 per month, or $63 per month billed yearly, with 60,000 units (adjustable up to 100,000), unlimited image concurrency, LoRA training on up to 2,000 images, and upscaling up to 22K. Business is $200 per month, or $160 per month billed yearly, with 80,000 units, up to 50 seats, and unlimited concurrency. Enterprise is custom-priced and is the only tier that adds SAML SSO, along with custom compute allowances and audit logs.

The main limits are practical. Everything is metered in compute units, so heavy use of video, 3D, or upscaling can burn through an allowance quickly, and the free daily cap is modest with no video access. The number of models and controls also makes the interface busy for newcomers, and higher concurrency or SSO require stepping up to the pricier plans.

Krea suits people who want one place for image, video, 3D, and upscaling rather than separate tools, and who value fast iteration and fine-grained control. It is less suited to anyone who only needs occasional single images and would rather not think about a credit system, or who needs SSO without paying for the custom Enterprise tier.

before.description_long:
Flux is a family of generative AI models built by Black Forest Labs, spanning top-tier API-only models and open-weight versions you can self-host and fine-tune. It originally focused on image generation and editing, but the company has since expanded well beyond images.

The current generation is FLUX 3, announced July 23, 2026, covering FLUX 3 Image, FLUX 3 Video (which adds native audio up to about 20 seconds), and FLUX 3 Action, an open-weights 7B model aimed at robotics, released September 2026. The earlier FLUX.2 lineup (pro, flex, max, dev, and the compact klein variant in 4B and 9B sizes, added January 2026) remains available, as do several legacy FLUX.1 tiers including Kontext Pro/Max and Pro Ultra.

Across the lineup, Flux models support multi-reference input (up to around 10 reference images) for character and style consistency, photorealistic image output up to 4 megapixels, and text rendering inside generated images. FLUX.2 [klein] is marketed as able to run on consumer hardware with sub-second inference. FLUX 3 Video adds synchronized audio generation.


Pricing is pay-as-you-go with no subscriptions or seat fees. FLUX 3 Image is billed per image: about $0.041 at 768 square, $0.048 at 1k, $0.100 at 2k, and $0.607 at 4k. FLUX 3 Video is billed per second, from roughly $0.06/s for drafts up to $0.17-$0.80/s depending on quality, with continuation generations at $0.41-$0.95/s. FLUX.2 lists starting per-image prices of about $0.014 (klein 4B), $0.015 (klein 9B), $0.03 (pro), $0.05 (flex), and $0.07 (max); the vendor's own pricing calculator has shown different default figures for some of these tiers, so exact per-image costs can vary. Legacy FLUX.1 tiers run roughly $0.04-$0.08 per image. Commercial self-hosting above certain volumes requires a separate annual Open Weights license (Builder, Platform, Professional, Enterprise tiers), with pricing not published on the vendor's pricing page.

There is no free hosted API tier; the only free route is self-hosting an open-weight model such as FLUX.1 [schnell] (Apache 2.0) within its license terms, since FLUX.1 [dev] remains non-commercial. The fast-expanding lineup, inconsistent per-image figures between docs and calculator, and license tiers for commercial self-hosting add complexity for buyers comparing options.

Flux suits developers and studios that want either top-tier image or video generation through an API, or a self-hostable, fine-tunable model, and that are comfortable with pay-per-asset billing or managing an open-weights license.

Pricing is organized into Free, Plus, Pro, and Ultra individual plans, plus Business and Enterprise options. The Free plan costs $0, includes 400 credits with no time limit, and requires no credit card; it keeps a Made with Gamma badge and allows up to 10 cards per prompt. Plus adds about 1,000 monthly credits and removes the badge; Pro adds roughly 4,000 monthly credits, API access, and up to 10 custom domains; Ultra adds about 20,000 monthly credits, API access, up to 100 custom domains, and its top-tier image models. Gamma's pricing page did not return per-seat dollar amounts for these three tiers at the time of review, so exact prices are not listed here; the help center notes that annual billing carries a 28% discount versus monthly billing. Business is confirmed at $40 per member per month, billed annually, with 6,000 monthly credits per member, SSO, SOC 2 documentation, 100 custom domains, and a locked training opt-out; no separate Team plan currently appears in Gamma's help articles. Enterprise pricing is custom and adds SCIM, audit logs, and invoiced billing.

Credits are consumed by AI generation, so heavy users can burn through an allowance quickly, and the Free plan's 400 credits are a fixed, one-time grant rather than a plan described as recurring. Because Gamma's public pricing page was inaccessible at the time of review, Plus, Pro, and Ultra dollar prices could not be independently confirmed. Fine visual control still lags behind traditional design tools.

Gamma suits people who need to produce decks, one-pagers, or landing pages fast and value speed over pixel-level control. It is a strong fit for founders, marketers, educators, and teams that want a consistent house style without a dedicated designer.

before.description_long:
OpenCode is an open-source coding agent built by Anomaly, published under MIT license at github.com/anomalyco/opencode (the project was previously hosted at sst/opencode). The current implementation is written in TypeScript. Unlike earlier terminal-only tools in this space, OpenCode is available as a terminal interface, a desktop app, and an IDE extension.

The project has a large, active user base: the GitHub repo has drawn over 208,000 stars and 950+ contributors across 13,000+ commits, and Anomaly states OpenCode is used by over 16 million developers every month.

OpenCode connects to 75+ LLM providers through Models.dev, including Claude, GPT, Gemini, and more, as well as local models. Instead of managing API keys, you can also log in with a GitHub Copilot account or a ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription. The tool supports running multiple agent sessions in parallel on the same project and generating shareable session links. It integrates LSP (Language Server Protocol) for real-time diagnostics and code intelligence. Anomaly states that OpenCode does not store any of your code or context data.

Pricing has two layers. The OpenCode agent itself is completely free and open source — you pay only for the LLM API calls you make to your chosen provider, or nothing if you run local models. Anomaly also offers OpenCode Zen, an optional first-party AI gateway of curated models billed per request against prepaid credits; no public per-model rate card was available at review time. A separate Enterprise tier is listed on the site but its terms are not published.

Limitations: no version number is currently published for the agent, so users cannot easily track release history. Some previously advertised details, such as a SQLite-backed client/server session persistence layer and a GitHub Actions '/opencode' comment trigger, could not be confirmed on the current site and are not included here. As with any agent, result quality depends heavily on which LLM you configure.

OpenCode suits developers who want a free, open-source, provider-agnostic coding agent that isn't locked into a single interface or vendor, with the option to pay only for a managed model gateway (Zen) if they'd rather not handle their own API keys.

before.description: Whisper is OpenAI's open-source speech-to-text model for transcription and translation. The latest open checkpoint is large-v3-turbo, an optimized version of large-v3 that runs roughly 8x faster with only a small accuracy trade-off.
before.description_long:
Whisper is a family of open-source speech recognition models released by OpenAI. It transcribes spoken audio into text and the multilingual large-v3 models can translate speech from many languages directly into English. The weights are published under the permissive MIT license, so you can download them and run them on your own hardware.

The current open release is large-v3-turbo, an optimized version of large-v3 released in September 2024. It keeps almost all of the accuracy of the full large-v3 model while running about 8x faster, which makes it far more practical for batch jobs and near-real-time use. The full large-v3 checkpoint is still available when you want the highest possible quality. Turbo itself is not trained for translation tasks; use the other multilingual large-v3 checkpoints for speech-to-English translation.

Alongside the open models, OpenAI offers hosted transcription through its API. The original endpoint, whisper-1, has been joined by newer models: gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, and gpt-transcribe, which OpenAI now recommends as the default for recorded speech. Speaker diarization is handled by a separate model, gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize, and live streaming is handled by gpt-live-transcribe, with gpt-realtime-whisper and gpt-realtime-translate also listed on OpenAI's pricing page.

Pricing splits into two tracks. The open-source models are free to use — you only pay for your own compute. The hosted API is billed per minute of audio: whisper-1 and gpt-4o-transcribe are $0.006/min, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe is $0.003/min, gpt-transcribe is $0.0045/min, gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize is $0.006/min, gpt-live-transcribe and gpt-realtime-whisper are $0.017/min, and gpt-realtime-translate is $0.034/min.

Accuracy varies a lot by language. Whisper was trained on around 99 languages, but quality is strongest for high-resource languages like English and drops noticeably for less common ones. Running the larger models locally also needs a capable GPU, and the model can occasionally hallucinate text during long silences.

Whisper is a good fit if you want a free, self-hostable transcription engine, need broad multilingual coverage, or want a managed API without building your own pipeline. Choose the hosted gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize or gpt-live-transcribe models if you need diarization or live streaming out of the box.

after.description: Whisper is OpenAI's open-source speech-to-text model for transcription and translation. The latest open checkpoint is large-v3-turbo, an optimized version of large-v3 that runs roughly 8x faster with only a small accuracy trade-off.
after.description_long:
Whisper is a family of open-source speech recognition models released by OpenAI. It transcribes spoken audio into text and the multilingual large-v3 models can translate speech from many languages directly into English. The weights are published under the permissive MIT license, so you can download them and run them on your own hardware.

The current open release is large-v3-turbo, an optimized version of large-v3 released in September 2024. It keeps almost all of the accuracy of the full large-v3 model while running about 8x faster, which makes it far more practical for batch jobs and near-real-time use. The full large-v3 checkpoint is still available when you want the highest possible quality. Turbo itself is not trained for translation tasks; use the other multilingual large-v3 checkpoints for speech-to-English translation.

Alongside the open models, OpenAI offers hosted transcription through its API. The original endpoint, whisper-1, along with gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize, were deprecated in August 2026 and are scheduled for removal from the API on February 26, 2027. OpenAI now recommends gpt-transcribe for file-based transcription and gpt-live-transcribe for live streaming audio. gpt-realtime-whisper and gpt-realtime-translate are also listed on OpenAI's pricing page.

Pricing splits into two tracks. The open-source models are free to use — you only pay for your own compute. The hosted API is billed per minute of audio: gpt-transcribe costs $0.0045/min, gpt-live-transcribe and gpt-realtime-whisper cost $0.017/min, and gpt-realtime-translate costs $0.034/min. The deprecated whisper-1, gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize models remain billable at their existing per-minute rates until they are removed on February 26, 2027.

Accuracy varies a lot by language. Whisper was trained on around 99 languages, but quality is strongest for high-resource languages like English and drops noticeably for less common ones. Running the larger models locally also needs a capable GPU, and the model can occasionally hallucinate text during long silences.

Whisper is a good fit if you want a free, self-hostable transcription engine, need broad multilingual coverage, or want a managed API without building your own pipeline. Choose the hosted gpt-transcribe or gpt-live-transcribe models if you need file-based or live transcription through OpenAI's API, and plan to migrate away from any integration still using the deprecated endpoints.

before.description_long:
Adobe Podcast is a web app for recording and cleaning up spoken-word audio without a traditional editing suite. Its best-known feature, Enhance Speech, strips background noise and room echo from voice recordings and makes them sound as if they were captured with a studio microphone.

A March 2026 update expanded Enhance Speech with source separation: you can independently adjust or remove background noise, isolate dialogue, and raise or lower background music with sliders, then download separate audio stems for speech, noise and music. The same update added remote recording and multitrack import support.

The Studio side of the product accepts multitrack audio and video uploads with automatic syncing, so podcast and interview recordings from several sources can be aligned and enhanced together.

Pricing is freemium. The free plan costs nothing but is audio-only with no video, no bulk uploads, files capped at 30 minutes and 500 MB, a one-hour-per-day enhancement limit, Studio downloads restricted to 30-minute projects twice a day, and no option to download the original recording. Advanced features are now sold as Adobe Firefly Pro at $19.99 per month, which bundles Podcast Premium: 4,000 generative credits a month, up to four hours of enhancement a day, files up to 1 GB, video support (MP4/MOV), batch uploads, adjustable speech/music/ambience strength, unlimited Studio downloads and speaker-separated stems. A free trial is offered. Some existing subscribers who joined under an older standalone $9.99-per-month Premium plan keep that pricing, but new signups go through Firefly Pro.

The main limitation is that the features most people want at scale, video, long files and bulk processing, sit behind the paid Firefly Pro tier, and the free daily caps are easy to hit in a real workflow.

It suits podcasters, interviewers, video creators and anyone who records voice in imperfect rooms and wants clean results fast; the free tier is fine for occasional short clips, while regular producers will need Firefly Pro.

before.description_long:
Relevance AI is a no-code platform for building and deploying AI agents and multi-agent teams. Its specialty is multi-agent orchestration — systems where specialized agents (a researcher, a writer, a QA reviewer) collaborate to complete complex workflows that a single agent could not handle reliably.

The company has repositioned toward enterprise buyers under an 'AI Workforce' framing. Its public pricing page now shows only an Enterprise tier with a 'Talk to sales' call to action and no published numbers. Self-serve Pro and Team pricing still appears on the vendor's documentation pages. There is no free plan: the vendor's own docs state the Free plan is retired for both new signups and existing accounts.

The platform includes a visual workflow builder, fine-tuning on company-specific documents, and multi-agent orchestration that handles task delegation, result aggregation, and quality checking automatically. Agents connect to CRM systems, databases, Slack, and email, and the Enterprise tier advertises 2,000+ integrations.

Pricing is split into two components: Actions (what agents do) and Vendor Credits (model costs, passed through at wholesale with no markup). Per the vendor's docs, Pro is $19/month billed annually or $29/month billed monthly, including 2,500 actions and $20 of vendor credits per month. Team is $234/month billed annually or $349/month billed monthly, including 7,000 actions and $70 of vendor credits per month, plus calling agents, meeting agents, and an analytics dashboard. Enterprise is custom, quoted via sales, and adds unlimited agents, users, and projects, 2,000+ integrations, enterprise triggers, agent evaluations, A/B testing, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and a dedicated account manager.

Limitations: steeper learning curve than simpler tools like Lindy; the Team tier is expensive for small teams; the shift to an Enterprise-only public pricing page makes self-serve buying less transparent; and the two-currency (actions plus credits) pricing model can confuse new users. Best for revenue operations, marketing automation, and support teams — and increasingly enterprise buyers — who need multi-agent workflows handling complex, multi-step business processes.

Copy.ai suits sales and marketing teams that want to automate go-to-market work with agents and workflows, and can justify team pricing. Individual writers who just want cheap copy generation have better-value options elsewhere.
